title: Rules about AI use at school and work

sections.skill: Find and follow the AI rules that apply, including disclosure

questions.prompt: Where should a student look first for AI rules on an assignment?

choices.text: The assignment instructions and syllabus
A friend's guess
The AI tool's advertising
A social media post from a student at a different school last year

questions.correct_answer: The assignment instructions and syllabus
questions.intro: Schools, teachers and workplaces set their own RULES about using AI, and those rules differ: one class may allow AI for brainstorming but not writing, another may ban it, and a workplace may allow only approved tools. Find the rule that applies (the syllabus, assignment instructions, school handbook or workplace policy), and ask when it is unclear. Many rules require DISCLOSURE: saying how you used AI ("I used an AI tool to check grammar"). Breaking a rule can count as academic dishonesty or a policy violation, even if the same use is allowed somewhere else.
questions.feedback: The applicable rules come from your class.

sections.skill: Compare AI rules with rules for calculators

questions.prompt: Why might calculators be banned on a mental math test?

choices.text: The test measures mental arithmetic
Calculators are too slow
Because calculators are always illegal in schools in every country
Calculators are expensive

questions.correct_answer: The test measures mental arithmetic
questions.intro: In math class, calculators are sometimes allowed and sometimes not. On a test about mental arithmetic, a calculator would defeat the purpose; on a physics test, it might be expected. The calculator is the same; the RULE depends on what the task is meant to measure. AI tools work the same way. A rule against AI on an essay may exist because the essay measures your writing, while AI might be welcome for research brainstorming in another class.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Handle layered rules and keep honest records

questions.prompt: A school allows AI, but one teacher bans it for a specific essay. Which rule governs that essay?

choices.text: Neither applies
The teacher's specific instruction
Whichever the student prefers
The general school policy

questions.correct_answer: The teacher's specific instruction
questions.intro: Rules can be layered and specific. A school policy might allow AI generally while one teacher forbids it for a particular assignment; the more specific instruction usually governs that assignment. A workplace might allow AI for internal drafts but not for anything sent to clients. When you disclose, be accurate and specific: what tool use, for which part. Keeping notes of how you used AI, such as the requests you made, makes honest disclosure easy and protects you if questions come up.

questions.prompt: A workplace allows AI for internal drafts but not for client messages. A draft becomes a client email. What should happen?

choices.text: Rewrite or review it to meet the client-message rule
Send it as is, since it started out as an internal draft and is therefore allowed
Send it without telling anyone
Delete the client
